APPEND under the 2026-10-18 S7b v3 in-place resume rules entry (unit s7b-2, stage B: the wiring and the final guards).

(10) The in-place resume is wired. `begin_continuation` selects the stage (`select_stage`, a downgrade is never a refusal and is logged as loop_resume_downgraded), makes the ONE consume, and for `loop` runs the scope check, a pre-claim writer check, the claim of `{run_id}:{consumed step}`, the pure fold checks, ONE ledger read and the rebuild. A restore failure falls back to stage 1 under the same consume (resume_fallback, no second consume, no close, no fold RPC); a denial, a ZDR refusal, a run that ended, a claim another request holds, a widened fold authority and a release the ledger already holds REFUSE with nothing dispatched. Every refusal up to and including the restore precedes the run's first heartbeat, and no executor refusal terminalizes the run.

(11) Inside run_rounds the restored round runs in this order, pinned by the durable_loop_contract guard `in_place_writer_violations`: the phase-1 walk (resolved calls keep their step and outcome and are not run through the pre-pass again; the released call and any safe-to-repeat call run every gate under their slot's step id and take no step_seq), then the FENCE (one `pre_effect` save at the claimed seq through the seeded writer; it stands in for the ordinary pre-effect save of that round), then the release's pre-reserve, then phase 2. A fence that cannot be written (stale, closed, unavailable, content refused) is resume_checkpoint_unavailable, a denial is resume_forbidden, a ZDR trailer is the catalogue refusal; a pre-reserve that errors or whose answer was lost is resume_checkpoint_unavailable in place (stage 1 keeps its held-back text); AlreadyReserved or an identity conflict is continuation_already_consumed in both stages. Nothing of the round is dispatched in any of these cases.

(12) One writer decision. The seeded writer's gate comes from the one `writer_gate` fn (its `resumed` flag reads `holds_release && !in_place`), and FoldWriter::seeded and resume::in_place_writer_off both force `resumed: false` themselves, so the pre-claim check and the writer cannot disagree. The `!in_place` is therefore behaviourally redundant and is held textually by the contract guard. A writer that would not be active is a downgrade to stage 1 BEFORE the claim (token writer_inactive), not a refusal after a won claim (the design's F16 is superseded).

(13) A fold that records a sibling which already ran keeps that sibling's original step id and its completed entry (fold_rejected writes each call's own step id); a call refused before dispatch keeps its empty step id; only the approved call carries the release's new step id and a safe-to-repeat call its new `s{N}.` id. A call with no step id, withheld arguments or no slot is never dispatched by a resume (`seeded_call`).

(14) Closed tokens after the consume and their codes: continuation_already_consumed, approval_not_resumable, approval_snapshot_mismatch, approval_action_mismatch, not_releasable, authority_widened, authority_space_mismatch, authority_route_mismatch and continue_space_scope_unsupported are FailedPrecondition; continue_in_progress is Aborted; not_resumable (run ended) is FailedPrecondition; resume_forbidden is PermissionDenied; resume_checkpoint_unavailable is FailedPrecondition; the ZDR refusal is the catalogue's own FailedPrecondition with its trailer; in_place_seed_invalid (defensive) is Internal.

findings.issue: preconsume_refusal flattens a zero-retention catalogue refusal on the consume (FailedPrecondition plus the ZDR kind trailer) to 409 `not_resumable` and drops the typed body. The design interface says ZDR typed refusals keep grpc_status_to_http's body. In normal flow the persistent gate refuses a ZDR caller first, so this is a race or skew path only. It is a requirement not met, and no test covers a trailer-carrying status on the consume map. The implementer's commit message lists it as known and queued.
findings.evidence: session-core retention_receipt::refuse_zdr_continuation returns Refusal::DURABLE_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN.grpc_status(Code::FailedPrecondition). preconsume_refusal matches Code::FailedPrecondition and falls to the `_ => "not_resumable"` arm because the message is not one of the three closed tokens. a_consume_refusal_maps_to_its_closed_http_code never builds a status with the trailer. The design says: 'ZDR typed refusals keep grpc_status_to_http's body'.

findings.issue: classify_continue_dispatch_failure is spend-agnostic. InvalidArgument, Unauthenticated and PermissionDenied from RunAgent are classified Refused(..) whether or not the gateway pre-consumed. The design (regime 3) says that without a pre-consume these three statuses must keep the committed confirmed-rejection arm, which terminalizes the run. Nothing in the type or the tests forces S7c-B1 to branch on the spend state. If B1 routes a non-pre-consumed continuation through this classifier, a confirmed rejection stops terminalizing.
findings.evidence: The function takes only &Status. The match arm `FailedPrecondition | Aborted | InvalidArgument | PermissionDenied | Unauthenticated` returns Refused for all five. The classification test a_refused_continuation_is_classified_without_terminalizing pins all five carriers with no regime. continue_failure_event is documented as spent-regime only, but classify is not.

Record the obligation in the plan ledger.

findings.issue: approval_spend_for(resume_enabled) returns SpentByGateway from the switch alone. Any caller that evaluates it before or without a won consume (a lost-consume or refusal path, or a request-construction failure computed up front) will tell the client `approval_spent: true` for a click that was not spent.
findings.evidence: fn approval_spend_for(resume_enabled: bool) -> ApprovalSpend { if resume_enabled { SpentByGateway } else { NotSpent } }. No type ties SpentByGateway to a won consume. Accepted change (WS03 S7c-A5 fix): the BFF's /api/v1/orchestration/runs/{run_id}/continue relay has no switch. findings.issue: chatRunContinueTransportFailureOf reads any plain object that has no numeric status as a failed request: spent unknown, retryable true, followRun true. That includes a successful `connected` frame, `{}`, a NaN status, and a regime-1 refusal frame that carries approval_spent:true. The doc says it is null 'for anything that is not an object', which implies every object is a failure. A caller that feeds a frame to it gets retryable:true where the frame guard says spent=yes and never retry.
findings.evidence: Ran the committed contract file under node: transport({}) , transport({ok:true,run_id:'r'}) and transport({status:NaN}) all return {kind:'transport',reason:'unlisted',approvalSpent:'unknown',retryable:true,followRun:true}. transport({code:'continue_disabled',approval_spent:true}) also returns retryable:true, while chatRunContinueFrameRefusalOf on the same value returns regime 1, yes, retryable false. The fall-through is the last line of the function: `transport(errorLike ? 'network' : 'unlisted')`.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the guard positive. Read an error only by shape: an ApiError or Error-like value, a numeric status >= 400, or the mid-stream upstream_unavailable envelope. Return null for any other object. Add tests for a connected frame, `{}`, NaN and a spent frame. Alternatively restrict its documented input to a value thrown by continueRun and say so.

findings.issue: The contract text overclaims coverage. Its header says the two guards 'read every failed request' and that 'a null from both means the value is not a failed request at all'. The continueRun doc lists 'a dropped connection' as read by the transport guard. That holds only for a fetch rejection or a reader.read() error. A user abort returns silently in readSseStream (AbortError). A clean EOF after the headers with no terminal frame also ends silently. continueRun then resolves normally, no guard sees anything, and the spend is unknown. This is the 'dropped stream' case the unit's own item 1 names. The commit message lists it as 'known and queued', but the committed wording says the opposite.
findings.evidence: src/shared/api/sse.ts: `if (err instanceof DOMException && err.name === 'AbortError') return` skips onError. A normal `done` ends the loop without any terminal-frame check. continueRun only throws connError, so abort and clean EOF resolve. The header comment and the continueRun doc comment in orchestration-client.ts still claim full coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the wording true now. Say that a stream that ends without a terminal frame, or that the caller aborts, resolves without throwing and has an unknown spend. Tell the UI wiring step to treat 'resolved without a terminal frame' as the same ambiguous class (follow the run). Better, add an explicit helper or flag for it, and add a test.

findings.issue: The new guidance contradicts itself. CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_AMBIGUOUS_FAILURE_GUIDANCE and the registry description say 'the run read is the arbiter'. CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_FOLLOW_RUN_NOTE admits that after continue_unavailable the click can be spent while no run was launched and the run stays parked. A run read of such a run looks like an untouched pause, so it cannot settle the spend. Only the same-token 409 does, and that may arrive after the 15 minute window. The registry description also says 'every consumed approval is refused with 409 continuation_already_consumed, the same token included'. A few sentences later it says not_resumable, approval_not_found and continue_disabled can also answer a spent approval. Both statements cannot be true.
findings.evidence: action-registry.ts, chat.run.continue description, versus CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_FOLLOW_RUN_NOTE. Gateway continue_preflight returns not_resumable for a completed, failed or cancelled run before it reads approval_consumed. consume_approval_with answers a replay on an ended run with NotFound before it checks consumed_at.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop 'arbiter'. Say that the run read shows what became of the run, not whether the approval was spent, and that the same-token retry (409 continuation_already_consumed) is the only signal that says spent. Reword the first sentence to 'a consumed approval is refused with 409 continuation_already_consumed unless the run has ended or the switch is off, when it gets not_resumable, approval_not_found or continue_disabled'. Update the tests that pin the exact strings.

findings.issue: The transport class is retryable:true and followRun:true for every unlisted failure. Many of these are deterministic refusals that did not spend anything and that a retry cannot fix. Examples are the BFF's own 400 continue_incomplete, a 401 unauthorized, a 403, a 412 or 500 model_error, and a gateway 502 or 504 from grpc_status_to_http on the owner, get_run or get_approval reads, which all happen before any consume. These are all labelled 'spent unknown, retry the same token', so a UI wired to the table would offer or run a retry that cannot succeed, and would send the user to follow a run that was never launched. The commit message admits this ('retryable for deterministic refusals that no retry can fix'). The contract does not say so.
findings.evidence: Probe: transport({status:401,code:'unauthorized'}) and transport({status:400,code:'continue_incomplete'}) both return retryable:true, approvalSpent:'unknown'. model-gateway grpc_status_to_http maps Unavailable to 502 and DeadlineExceeded to 504 for the pre-consume reads, with a flat body.

Or split out the statuses that are certain to be pre-send (400, 401, 403) as unspent. Pin the table row by row as is done for the listed codes.

findings.issue: The 'no' rows (approval_not_granted, approval_expired, approval_not_resumable) rest on the order of checks in session-core consume_approval_with: the consumed_at check comes before the grant, expiry and descriptor checks.
